rationale: The current three-file diff was inspected together with the membership repository, User access helpers, router wiring and PostgreSQL ingestion gate call sites. Database-managed non-admin senders must have a current user/project row before any analytics persistence. The lookup uses the canonical stored project name and the authenticated user id, and database errors retain the existing unavailable/retry path. Global administrator and legacy IDP behavior remain unchanged. No blocking findings were identified in this bounded change.
checks: Current membership is queried in the existing async project-lookup session; no shared authentication-cache changes are introduced.
A removed member or project administrator is rejected despite a stale positive User access snapshot.
The ingest gate runs before persistence for both OTel signals and hook events; rejection leaves canonical_project unset.
Regression tests observe rejection and absence of storage writes for all supported endpoint/wire formats, and cover membership-lookup failure, legacy mode and global administrator access.

evidence.targeted_backend_tests: 145 passed, 2 warnings in 9.40s; existing run, not rerun for this review artifact.
evidence.live_standalone: Four revocations and sixteen immediate ingest requests were verified with the same cached token; rejected sessions were absent and positive controls remained readable.
evidence.baseline: The original acceptance bug and the two unrelated sanity outcomes were reproduced on exact main baseline 9beb32e9a7e7e562738f2d7c0a4e424c601d844b.
evidence.rebase: git range-diff confirmed the functional patch was unchanged when rebased from e9cb3cc51 to 9ddf82521.

limitations: This is a scoped self-review, not a GitLab human approval or a fresh full test run.
Requests authorized before membership removal commits are not cancelled; global-role revocation and legacy IDP token lifetime are outside this fix.
